npcs.name: Garanki Gabu
npcs.bio: Mao'ao professor of Ikiology (anthropology) from the Tower of Learning in Kumapirra, drawn to the Highlands by its unstudied ruins and uncatalogued wildlife. Cheerful, a little oblivious to how remote he really is.
npcs.loreBackground: Garanki came to the Highlands because the region has never been properly catalogued — too remote, too dangerous, and too unprofitable for most academics to bother with. He's effectively self-funding the expedition out of his Researcher's Tent and writes up every donation to mail back to the Tower. <suggestion: backstory — does he have a sponsor, a rival academic back home, or a reason this trip matters more than a normal sabbatical?>
questHooks: Accepts donations of Relics, Flora, Fish, and Minerals; each new donation raises the town's [Trade Value] as he mails findings back to the Tower of Learning.
<suggestion: quest design — define the donation tiers/milestones and what unlocks at each Trade Value threshold from his findings specifically>

npcs.name: Kzubug
npcs.bio: Late-middle-aged Mashtzarr smith, broad and gentle despite the trade. Fiercely protective of his adopted daughter Sloomi — losing his whole birth family to plague left him treating her like a second chance he refuses to risk losing.
npcs.loreBackground: SPOILER — not for casual player-facing dialogue. Sloomi is the half-sister of Jubmir the trader. Jubmir's father Slorik was a trader who got injured near Hobunji and was taken in by Kzubug's family. Slorik saw how loving Kzubug's household was and wanted that for himself, despite having already been chosen to sire one son (Jubmir) with the Doromabi of his home village. Slorik returned to a guard job near Jubmir in secret, fell in love with Jubmir's Mabinga, Yanmira, and the two eloped into the Slagothi'ey wilderness with Jubmir when Yanmira became pregnant with Sloomi. When the Doromabi found their hideout, Yanmira and Slorik were killed; Jubmir escaped with infant Sloomi on his father's last instructions, found Dugmir (an old trade-route friend of Slorik's), and had Sloomi delivered to Kzubug while Jubmir himself returned to his Doro as the only one who hadn't committed or resulted from a crime. By the time Sloomi arrived, plague had wiped out Kzubug's whole family, so he took her in as divine providence and has been overprotective of her ever since. Jubmir knows the full story; Sloomi does not. It's the biggest reason Jubmir keeps making his barely-profitable trade runs to Hobunji. <suggestion: backstory — the plague's name/cause, the exact timeline (years since), and whether/when Sloomi ever learns the truth>

entries.text: Morning, {{pool:Kzubug Nicknames}}. Forge is hot if your tools need tending.

npcs.name: Sloomi
npcs.bio: Kzubug's adopted Slagothim apprentice; soft-spoken most of the time, but turns fierce if anyone she cares about is hurt, physically or emotionally. Doesn't know who her birth parents were.
npcs.loreBackground: See Kzubug's loreBackground for the full secret — Sloomi is Jubmir's half-sister and doesn't know it. <suggestion: dialogue writing — how close dialogue can get to the truth before it would need to actually reveal it, and whether there's a reveal questline planned>

entries.text: Hello, {{pool:Sloomi Nicknames}}. I can look at your tools, if you want.
Good evening, {{pool:Sloomi Nicknames}}. The forge is finally quiet.

npcs.name: Hreesh Nakheez

entries.text: Sit down, {{pool:Hreesh Nicknames}}. Or don't. Just quit blocking the way.

npcs.name: Jubmir
npcs.bio: The only Slagothim trader who still bothers with Hobunji's bi-weekly sell, despite the route barely turning a profit — he keeps coming because he genuinely cares about the village. Secretly half-Slagothim nobility by blood, though almost no one here knows it.
npcs.loreBackground: Full secret backstory shared with Kzubug's entry: Jubmir is Sloomi's half-brother, son of the trader Slorik and a Doromabi he was chosen to mate with. After Slorik died eloping with Yanmira (Sloomi's mother), Jubmir carried infant Sloomi to safety, arranged for her to be raised by Kzubug, and returned alone to his Doro. Sloomi does not know this; Jubmir does, and it's the core reason he keeps risking the unprofitable trade route to Hobunji. He's also secretly protecting the Hakaru twins: he buys newspapers from other traders at an inflated price, resells them after removing any mention of the twins' bounty, and Father Hunundi quietly reimburses part of his losses out of his own temple salary. <suggestion: backstory — what Jubmir's life is like back among the Slagothim — does he have his own Doro/family obligations waiting, and does he resent them?>
questHooks: Currently the only trader willing to make the Hobunji run; stays only 2 days a week and sells on a bi-weekly cycle at game start.
His visit frequency and time spent in town scale up with the town's [Trade Value] — eventually attracting other Slagothim traders too.
<suggestion: quest design — the exact Trade Value thresholds for each increase in Jubmir's visit frequency/duration, and what unlocks when other traders start showing up>

entries.text: Good morning, {{pool:Jubmir Nicknames}}! I was hoping I'd find you well.
Good to see that you're still here, {{pool:Jubmir Nicknames}}.

npcs.name: Father Hunundi Hodu
npcs.bio: Late middle-aged Life Priest who runs the village's morning service on <suggestion: schedule — the design notes literally leave this weekday blank — pick one>. Gentle and quietly protective of anyone in trouble, including the Hakaru twins.

rules.activity: watching the Spirit Counsel from a far pew

npcs.loreBackground: Shelters the wanted Hakaru twins (Namu'i and Taku'a) at the temple and actively works with Jubmir to keep news of their bounty from reaching the villagers — Jubmir overpays for newspapers elsewhere and resells them with the bounty mentions removed, and Father Hunundi reimburses part of that loss out of his own salary. Also present (but not leading) during Eldress Teacup's nightly spirit communion services for the Engh-sho villagers, mostly to keep the other races at ease. <suggestion: backstory — how he first found the twins / decided to protect them, and how long this arrangement with Jubmir has been running>
questHooks: <suggestion: quest design — does the player ever learn about the twins' bounty / the Jubmir arrangement through Father Hunundi specifically, or only through the twins themselves?>

entries.text: A gentle morning to you, {{pool:Hunundi Nicknames}}.
Life keep you, {{pool:Hunundi Nicknames}}. How is your spirit today?
A peaceful evening to you, {{pool:Hunundi Nicknames}}.
Welcome, {{playerName}}. There is always a place for you here.

npcs.name: Namu’i u Hakaru
npcs.bio: Long-orphaned Kenkari twin who came to Hobunji looking for a normal life. Wanted, with a sizable bounty on her head, but truly wants to live an honest life rather than run from it.
npcs.loreBackground: Staying at the temple under Father Hunundi's protection alongside her brother Taku'a. Most villagers are wary rather than hateful — they just won't risk hiring a suspected criminal — except Kinami Kunji, who has it out for her specifically. <suggestion: backstory — what she and Taku'a actually did to earn the bounty, and how large it is>
questHooks: <suggestion: quest design — what kind of work would let her start paying off her own bounty, and what happens once it's paid>

entries.text: Morning, {{pool:Namui Nicknames}}. Quiet so far. That's good.
Ah, {{playerName}}! Thank the Breath! I'm glad it's just you.

npcs.name: Taku’a ao Hakaru
npcs.bio: Long-orphaned Kenkari twin, brother to Namu'i. Wanted alongside her, hoping to find honest work to pay off his own bounty. Becomes the village's miner once the Old Mine's first layer is cleared.
npcs.loreBackground: <suggestion: backstory — what specifically drives Taku'a toward mining once given the chance, and how that differs from Namu'i's path>
questHooks: Becomes the village miner NPC after the Old Mine's layers 1–20 boss is cleared and the tunnel collapse opens the next layer.

npcs.name: Kaboku Kunji
npcs.bio: Old man at the Potion Shop; kind-hearted and giving by nature, and lets his wife Kinami boss him around without complaint. He and Kinami had a falling out a few years ago and now avoid sharing a room except at dinner and bedtime.
npcs.loreBackground: <suggestion: backstory — what the falling out was actually about, and whether his passivity is contentment, exhaustion, or something sadder>

entries.text: Good morning, {{pool:Kaboku Nicknames}}. Can I brew you something helpful?
Welcome, {{pool:Kaboku Nicknames}}. Please, take whatever time you need.
Good evening, {{pool:Kaboku Nicknames}}. Mind the bottles in the dark.

npcs.name: Kinami Kunji
npcs.bio: Potion Shop resident; spiteful, racist, and an inveterate gossip who bosses her husband Kaboku around. Has a particular vendetta against the Hakaru twins. She and Kaboku had a falling out a few years ago and now avoid sharing a room except at dinner and bedtime.
npcs.loreBackground: The strongest voice of suspicion against Namu'i and Taku'a Hakaru — her instincts about them happen to be correct (they are wanted thieves), which only fuels her certainty about everyone else she distrusts. <suggestion: backstory — what specifically she says about other races/villagers, calibrated to be hateful without making her a cartoon — and whether anyone in town ever pushes back on her>

entries.text: Morning, {{pool:Kinami Nicknames}}. You're up late for a farmer.
Evening, {{pool:Kinami Nicknames}}. People do become careless after dark.
{{playerName}}. I suppose you've come for something. As your people often do.

Holds it in the temple building at night, since it tends to unsettle the other races. Lives with her son Spearhead and grandson Oddclaw in the overcrowded Unumanuk household.

rules.activity: leading the Spirit Counsel, eyes lowered

npcs.loreBackground: Father Hunundi attends her nightly services without leading them, mostly to keep the other villagers at ease and to be present in case 'something goes awry.' <suggestion: backstory — what spirit communion actually involves mechanically, and what 'going awry' has historically meant> The Unumanuk household is crammed well past what it was built for — three generations of Unumanuks plus <suggestion: household detail — which other displaced/immigrant families share the house, and why they ended up here> share the single building, with most of the floor given over to bedrolls rather than beds.

entries.text: Soft morning, {{pool:Nohuknuk Nicknames}}. The snow remembers your footsteps.
Ahhh, {{pool:Nohuknuk Nicknames}}. Have you come to ask winter for a favor?
Blue evening, {{pool:Nohuknuk Nicknames}}. Even the cold must settle down.
I know your tread, {{playerName}}. Every snowbank knows it.

npcs.name: Hiki-hiki
npcs.species: <suggestion: species — a talking, hat-wearing Drenkiira trickster — not one of the six playable rigs, needs a custom model>
npcs.gender: <suggestion: gender — not specified in the design doc>
npcs.bio: A talking, hat-wearing Drenkiira trickster who sends visitors on a scavenger hunt of riddles to figure out what offering he actually wants. Swaps his current hat for a new one every time you guess correctly.

scheduleHooks.contentIncompleteReason: defaultPosition is a placeholder {0,0} — this NPC spawns (or falls back) to world origin whenever no schedule rule is active. Needs a real station.

npcs.loreBackground: Each correct offering earns the player his current hat and reveals a new riddle pointing toward the next offering. <suggestion: quest design — the full riddle text and answers, how many offerings the chain has, and what the collected hats are used for>
questHooks: Each successful offering triggers the next riddle and a hat swap.
<suggestion: quest design — the riddle chain content and whether the retired hats become wearable cosmetics for the player>

entries.text: Morning, {{pool:Hiki-hiki Nicknames}}! Or is it? Solve that first.
Hiki-hiki sees you, {{pool:Hiki-hiki Nicknames}}! But which hat sees you best?
Evening, {{pool:Hiki-hiki Nicknames}}. Riddles grow teeth after dark.
{{playerName}}! I have exactly what you want, if you guess what I want.

npcs.name: Banubu
npcs.species: <suggestion: species — the 'Sleepy Grehlr' — glowing green eyes, perpetual mist; not one of the six playable rigs, needs a custom model>
npcs.gender: <suggestion: gender — not specified in the design doc>
npcs.bio: The Sleepy Grehlr — glowing green eyes, perpetual mist, living in a ruin-filled cave overlooking the river. Too tired to help because he's too hungry to hunt, and too hungry because he's too tired to hunt.

scheduleHooks.contentIncompleteReason: defaultPosition is a placeholder {0,0} — this NPC spawns (or falls back) to world origin whenever no schedule rule is active. Needs a real station.

npcs.loreBackground: Needs a 'Fifteen Fish Pie' to get the energy to help — quite literally fifteen different fish, each one only catchable in a specific season + weather + time + location combination around the town's outskirts. <suggestion: quest design — the actual list of fifteen fish and their catch conditions, plus the pie recipe itself>
questHooks: Requires a Fifteen Fish Pie built from fish that are each catchable only in one specific season/weather/time/location combination.
<suggestion: quest design — full fish list, catch conditions, and recipe>

entries.text: Oh... hello, {{pool:Banubu Nicknames}}. Wake me if you brought food.
Evening already, {{pool:Banubu Nicknames}}? I nearly got up.
{{playerName}}... you look energetic. Could you hunt something for me?

npcs.name: Mother Rahayobi
npcs.species: <suggestion: species — a hag who appears as an old Harlyao woman — clarify if she's truly Harlyao or just wears that appearance>
npcs.bio: A hag who appears as an old Harlyao woman. Agrees readily to drive off the Ghost Army — she has her own reasons — and has a multi-stage potion plan to do it.

scheduleHooks.contentIncompleteReason: defaultPosition is a placeholder {0,0} — this NPC spawns (or falls back) to world origin whenever no schedule rule is active. Needs a real station.

npcs.loreBackground: Her potion needs separate mixtures made from foragables and animal parts from every zone × weather × season combination; rare animal parts can be bought directly (expensively) from Bird Bone. Each turned-in mixture teaches the player a free set of special potion recipes. <suggestion: quest design — her real motive for wanting the Ghost Army gone, the full mixture list/recipes, and exactly which special potions each mixture unlocks>
questHooks: Multi-stage potion quest: separate mixtures per zone × weather × season combination.
Each submitted mixture teaches the player a new special potion recipe for free.
<suggestion: quest design — her real motive, full mixture/recipe list, and taught potions>

entries.text: Morning, {{pool:Rahayobi Nicknames}}. Dew gathers before sensible folk wake.
Come closer, {{pool:Rahayobi Nicknames}}. I only bite ingredients.
Evening, {{pool:Rahayobi Nicknames}}. A proper hour for unpleasant remedies.
{{playerName}}. Have you brought what the dead would rather I lacked?

entries.text: Morning, {{pool:Baruhi Leader Nicknames}}. Stand straight when you enter my camp.
Speak, {{pool:Baruhi Leader Nicknames}}. The Baruhi have no time for trembling.
Evening, {{pool:Baruhi Leader Nicknames}}. Cross no boundary you cannot defend.
{{playerName}}. Have you come as witness, messenger, or enemy?

entries.text: Morning, {{pool:Porakaneki Leader Nicknames}}. Choose your words before you cross our fire.
You stand before the Porakaneki, {{pool:Porakaneki Leader Nicknames}}. Speak plainly.
Evening, {{pool:Porakaneki Leader Nicknames}}. Our watch does not sleep.
{{playerName}}. Do you bring truth, or another tribe's version of it?

entries.text: A productive morning, {{pool:Khannibarri Agent Nicknames}}. Shall we discuss opportunity?
Welcome, {{pool:Khannibarri Agent Nicknames}}. Khannibarri values proactive partners.
Working late, {{pool:Khannibarri Agent Nicknames}}? Admirable. Potentially billable.
{{playerName}}! Precisely the stakeholder I hoped to see.

entries.text: Good morning, {{pool:Village Leader Nicknames}}. Hobunji needs all of us today.
Hello, {{pool:Village Leader Nicknames}}. Is there a village matter I should hear?
Good evening, {{pool:Village Leader Nicknames}}. Another difficult day behind us.
{{playerName}}. I hope your farm is weathering the shortage.
